reasoning_traces.think:
The OpenSkill framework implements a Bayesian approximation to TrueSkill using the Weng-Lin formulation, enabling fast, scalable multi-team, asymmetric game ranking. It assumes Gaussian skill distributions and models performance as skill plus noise. The Plackett-Luce model provides a likelihood function for ordinal outcomes in multi-team settings. Each player maintains a μ (mean skill) and σ (uncertainty), which update post-match via Bayesian inference. Asymmetry is handled by adjusting likelihood functions for team size differences and partial play. The system supports time decay through σ inflation. Its primary limitation is lack of per-player contribution weighting within teams. In practice, this enables GSE to maintain real-time team strength states and GSI to compute uncertainty-adjusted predictions. Failure modes include underfitting in sparse data regimes and overfitting when team sizes vary widely without proper normalization.
